content:
Romansh was elevated to the status of a national language of Switzerland through a popular vote in **1938**.

Following the revision of the language article in the Swiss Constitution in **1996**, Romansh's official status was formally recognized as one of the four national languages of Switzerland, alongside German, French, and Italian. It is officially used in correspondence with Romansh-speaking citizens and has specific provisions for its use in certain administrative districts of the canton of Graubünden.
